input.quote: The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no licence grant: the only "licen[cs]e" references are regulatory qualification representations (p0234, p0259, p0272) and the Section 7.5(b) sentence at p0346, which disclaims any obligation on the Servicer to provide, license or assign its servicing software or applications. As drafted that leaves us with no licensed rights, no route to extend rights to our Affiliates and nothing transferable on a merger or acquisition, which is the walk-away outcome, so this is a deviation. We took the fallback level and made the change by addition rather than deletion: a single new sentence granting the Issuer and Depositor a licence to use the Servicer's processes, procedures, models, servicing software and other applications as necessary to service, or to have serviced, the Receivables, extended to their respective Affiliates on written notice and transferable to a successor of the Issuer or Depositor by merger or acquisition. "Affiliate" is a defined term at p0579, so no undefined capitalised term is introduced. Following the verifier's minimality point, the Servicer's existing carve-out is now retained word for word, including the Successor Servicer and third-party allocation and the restriction/confidentiality/legal, regulatory, privacy and data protection protections; the new sentence displaces it only to the extent of this grant, and I no longer assert that the Section 7.4/7.5 transition allocation is untouched, since the override operates on that sentence. We stopped at the fallback and did not add contractor coverage, perpetuity, irrevocability, termination-only-for-uncured-material-breach or unqualified transferability.

proposal.summary: Add a short licence sentence after Section 7.5(b) granting the Issuer and Depositor rights in the Servicer's servicing software, extended to their Affiliates on written notice and transferable to an M&A successor, leaving the existing Successor Servicer/third-party carve-out fully intact.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a licence to use the Servicer's servicing software and related applications, extended to our Affiliates on written notice and transferable to a successor by merger or acquisition, which is our fallback licence position. The Servicer's existing carve-out for Successor Servicers, third parties and restricted or confidential materials is left in place and is overridden only to the extent of this grant.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, the Servicer grants the Issuer and the Depositor, and on written notice their respective Affiliates, a license to use its processes, procedures, models, servicing software and other applications as necessary to service, or to have serviced, the Receivables, which license is transferable to a successor of the Issuer or the Depositor by merger or acquisition.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
